S036-01.notes: Nascent = just beginning; fits ~8,000 registered cars and handmade workshop production. Obsolete/regulated/consolidated contradict or are unsupported. The ~8,000 cars in 1900 figure is the standard cited number.

S036-02.notes: Old car, lunches with junior staff, crediting colleagues = unassuming; 'Although' contrast with fame confirms it.

S036-03.notes: Sentence 2 = microscope finding of hooks catching loops, the basis of the invention. B, C, D describe sentences 3, 1, 4. Facts (1941 walk, Swiss engineer, patent granted in 1950s) are accurate.

S036-04.notes: Ana wanted a new coat, then pictures her sister mending it and wears it all day: appreciation. A ignores the shift; B and D are not in the text.

flags: minor: B is true and partially relevant, but it does not compare near and far seedlings, so it does not support the full claim
S036-05.notes: The conclusion is comparative (near vs. far). Only D shows survival rising with distance, 12% to 51%. A and C each give a single group.

flags: minor: key is slightly the longest choice
S036-06.notes: Self-control was linked to learning ability, so delay capacity may relate to cognition beyond feeding. C overstates ('any... at all'), D reverses the relationship, and A contradicts the stated preference. Matches Schnell et al. 2021 (king prawn vs. live grass shrimp; longer waiters learned faster).

flags: minor: key is the longest choice
S036-07.notes: Guilty behavior tracked scolding, not whether the dog actually ate the treat, which undercuts the owners' inference. B misstates the result. Accurately reflects Horowitz 2009.

flags: minor: D also loosely introduces the record and its purpose, but it never names the Golden Records or their contents, so C is clearly better
S036-08.notes: C names the records and gives the date, the contents and the purpose, which suits an unfamiliar audience. A assumes the reader already knows 'the records', and B is about the spacecraft. Facts (1977, 55 languages, 115 images, gold-plated copper, left the heliosphere) are accurate.

S036-09.notes: Parallel series after 'can': climb, open, carry.

S036-10.notes: Possessive relative pronoun before 'team': whose. Inserting who's, who or whom makes the sentence ungrammatical.
